reviewer: Claude (2026-10-25), second pass: the 27 sheets not in review.json, so all 39 sheets (231 completion videos) are reviewed

families.locomotion and stance (02-05): Turns and moving turns, the Karnaca slope with guards, stairs, crouched idle, crouched movement in eight directions, crouch transitions, leans. Planted feet and stance changes.
families.airborne (06, 07): Standing and running take-offs, the double jump in the air, falls, soft and hard landings (the crouched landing on the docks).
families.traversal (09): The chain climb in Karnaca, swimming and diving. In the water frames the body is mostly under the surface and hard to see.
families.combat (10, 12, 13, 15): Light, heavy, crouched and moving attacks, counterattacks in a Karnaca street fight, hit reactions, a knockdown with the player on the floor and getting up, death collapses, the ragdoll handoff, pistol aim.
families.items and takedowns (17, 19, 21-25): Item switches, Emily's crossbow at the docks, lethal, non-lethal and crouched takedowns paired with guards, the window takedown with a Howler pulled over the sill, takedowns on other body sizes (civilians, palace guards at night, a hound), a first-person grab, a choke in a bar, carrying a body over the shoulder, a guard's grab with the struggle and escape.
families.powers (26, 29-32): Blink aim, cancel and arrive, the Blink pull, Mesmerize's spirit, Shadow Walk's crawling form, upgrades in a fight, Devouring Swarm rats, a second Emily from Doppelganger, the possession view, casts without mana and interrupted casts.
families.interactions and scenes (32, 34-36, 38): Doors pushed open with both arms, looting a guard, using a key, reading notes at a bookshelf and a desk, eating at a table, dialogue gestures at the black-market counter, the pump crank, scene pose handoffs, the Dreadful Wale's skiff after a map load.

issues: None that contradict an item's recorded verdict. Water and night frames are dark, and some frames catch the character out of shot mid-move; three frames per video do not show timing or blending, which rest on the recorded per-video verdicts.
